gap: The composition finally lands (block is vertically centered, field capped near a 450px measure, Continue is a compact pill), so r2 and r3 are closed. What loses it now is craft at close range, which is exactly where a finance signup earns trust. (1) The apostrophe in the 60px serif headline "What's your company name?" is a straight typewriter quote, not a typographic one, and it is the single largest piece of type on the page; Wave uses a proper curly apostrophe everywhere it speaks ("We're", "isn't", "It's Pro time"). (2) The only brand anchor on the page is a soft raster logo in rgb(60,123,190), a fourth blue that matches neither the headline navy rgb(13,27,94) nor the CTA rgb(22,80,238); Wave's wordmark is crisp vector in rgb(0,27,102), i.e. its own headline navy, so the mark reads as part of the system instead of a pasted asset. (3) The right-hand card is padded rather than persuasive: "Languages supported 5" and "Currency billing / Any" are not facts anyone decides on, and the closing paragraph restates the FREE chip and the "< 5 min" row directly above it, so three of five rows are said twice. Wave's equivalent panel always carries the number the reader is actually weighing ($0, $190 USD/year, Billed annually). Fix: swap the headline apostrophe to U+2019 site-wide, ship the logo as SVG recolored to the headline navy, and replace the two filler rows with the two facts that de-risk signup (what happens to data if you stop paying, and that no card is taken now), deleting the duplicated closing paragraph.
